retrieval_query: Explain breadth-first search versus depth-first search using the lecture notes.
answer:
Both breadth-first search and depth-first search can find a solution if one exists, provided the state space is not too large. [S1]

Depth-first search may waste time exploring very deep branches without a solution. [S1]

Breadth-first search is very demanding on memory because it must store all unexpanded nodes at a given level, whereas depth-first search only stores the current path. [S1]

Depth-first search does not generally find the shortest path; for example, in a route from S to G, breadth-first yields S-B-G while depth-first yields S-A-C-G. [S3]
